scientific_question: When DeepAA is retrained independently on the same leak-free HAM10000 split, does it recover consistent archetypal semantics after accounting for archetype permutation?

primary_scope.reference_selection: predetermined; never selected from validation or test appearance/performance

training_configuration.preprocessing: JPEG RGB decode; bilinear 128x128 resize; float32 divide by 255; no augmentation
training_configuration.evidence_note: Values are explicitly frozen for this proposed experiment from the final source defaults, README commands, committed table8 loss strings, and Gate 0 checkpoint evidence. Their historical status remains classified in repro/configs/conference_runs.json.

alignment.signal: per-image archetype coefficient columns in fixed manifest order
alignment.constant_or_nearly_inactive_column_rule: OPEN; analysis must stop for affected comparison until reviewed

held_out_evaluation.data: journal_v1 test only after validation alignment
held_out_evaluation.semantic: coefficient-weighted P(dx|matched archetype), compared with base-2 Jensen-Shannon divergence
held_out_evaluation.nearest_real: top-10 test images by Euclidean distance between mu and the corresponding raw fixed vertex; matched-set Jaccard overlap plus diagnosis-distribution consistency
held_out_evaluation.visual: decode each run's raw fixed vertices deterministically, then compare after alignment; exact image-similarity metric is OPEN pending review

not_permitted_in_v1: reference selection based on appearance or metrics
matching by Euclidean distance between fixed simplex vertices
changing the baseline architecture or objective
silently replacing the reference rule with consensus matching
